Area.evidence_source: Although there was evidence of an impulsive quality to some of the suicidal actions the men generally had been thinking about suicide for some time, often for years. Their intent in almost all cases was to end their lives and the outcome for any of them could have been death. A variety of methods were used but over-dosing with prescribed drugs was the most usual means. When they realised they were alive their reactions varied, although the majority were glad to be alive. The main reasons given by them for their actions included generalised unhappiness, being trapped in a situation, a relationship break-up, psychiatric symptoms and anger.
